terms.grammar: adjective; comparative crēbrior; adverb crēbrō, often
evidence: Caes. BG 5.45: tantō crēbriōrēs litterae nūntiīque (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of things that come one after another: letters, blows, rumours, visits. Of things in space it means thick, close together (crēbrae arborēs), the opposite of rārus.

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending; adverb frequenter
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 16: erat ille Rōmae frequēns (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Or. 4.45: frequēns … Platōnis audītor (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a person who is often in a place or often does a thing, a regular (frequēns audītor, a regular listener). Its other common sense is crowded, full (frequēns senātus, a full senate; Liv. 1.9.9, a city frequentem tēctīs).

phrases.latin: signumque aput tāleam adpōnitō crēbrōque sarītō, sī volēs citō sēmina crēscant
phrases.english: put a marker by the cutting and hoe often, if you want the seedlings to grow fast
do write as often as you can

phrases.latin: cum situm moeniaque et frequentem tēctīs urbem vīdissent
phrases.english: when they had seen the site, the walls and the city full of houses
